title: SQL Learning Path — Foundation to Senior
meta_description: SQL course path from foundation to senior DE level — 10 modules with guided checkpoints.
html:
Project EngineeringAtlas
LearnPracticeReferencesProgress
Project Engineering AtlasLearn

Goal: build complex SQL independently

The 10 modules provide the foundation. B01–B08 teach output grain → feature CTEs → JOINs → fixture checks.

Start B01–B08 →View progress →
PROJECT ENGINEERING ATLAS · SQL COURSE

SQL Learning Path
Foundation → Senior

This is a course path, not just a question bank. Each module moves through a lesson map → guided checkpoint → applied/repo reasoning → senior edge case. Once you understand the concepts, move on to the 100-question + 24-incident assessment.

0 / 10 modules understood
Stage 1 · Foundation

Syntax, output, execution order, small fixture.

Stage 2 · Applied/Repo

Grain, business rule, repo bridge, validation.

Stage 3 · Senior

Failure mode, RCA, idempotency, reconciliation, optimization.

Pass rule

Do not mark a module complete just because you memorised the answer. Mark it when you can: explain expected grain → predict edge case → choose validation → defend fix.

M01

DDL, Constraints & Keys

M01 DDL / Constraints / Keys

Foundation

Structure, constraints, key types, and grain.

Applied / Repo

Use grain to design uniqueness/business keys.

Senior

Schema contracts, natural vs surrogate keys, NULL/uniqueness semantics.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q001 · Ansh CP1

NOT NULL contract

stores_new.store_name is NOT NULL. What happens when an insert supplies only store_id=3?

Why this matters

NOT NULL rejects a row that does not supply a value for a required column without a default.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q005 · Olist grain evidence

Grain to key bridge

The order-item grain is one row per (order_id, order_item_id). Which constraint best matches that rule?

Why this matters

Composite uniqueness encodes the stated grain.

Provenance: source+repo bridge

SENIOR · Q007 · Repo grain reasoning

A constraint is not the entire contract

A table has a PRIMARY KEY, but the pipeline can still produce business duplicates. Why?

Why this matters

Senior review must distinguish physical uniqueness from business grain and pipeline stage.

Provenance: extension

M02

SELECT, WHERE, LIKE & ORDER BY

M02 SELECT / WHERE / LIKE / ORDER BY

Foundation

Projection, filters, precedence, LIKE, sorting, aliases.

Applied / Repo

Translate business filters explicitly and predict result rows.

Senior

Filter placement, deterministic ordering, sargability, portability.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q009 · Ansh CP2

WHERE filters rows

Which clause filters rows before GROUP BY?

Why this matters

WHERE filters input rows before grouping.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q013 · Ansh CP2

Silent AND/OR leak

Rule boss: female AND (France OR joined after 2022-01-01). What is the risk query `gender="F" AND country="France" OR join_date>...`?

Why this matters

Because `(F AND France) OR recent`, recent rows are no longer required to be female.

Provenance: source

SENIOR · Q016 · Optimization contract

Filter early caveat

Is “filter as early as possible” always correct?

Why this matters

The correctness contract comes first; pushdown is valid only if semantics are preserved.

Provenance: extension

M03

GROUP BY, Aggregates & HAVING

M03 GROUP BY / Aggregate / HAVING

Foundation

Aggregate functions, grouping, HAVING and execution order.

Applied / Repo

Define output grain before aggregation.

Senior

Reconciliation by grain; detect aggregation hiding duplicate problems.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q019 · Ansh CP2

GROUP BY grain

What grain does `GROUP BY category` produce?

Why this matters

Group key determines output grain aggregate.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q022 · Creative reconciliation reasoning

Reconciliation by grain

Total sales match, but one store is missing and another is duplicated. What is the lesson?

Why this matters

Reconciliation need both aggregate and key-level checks.

Provenance: extension+repo

SENIOR · Q025 · Join/cardinality reasoning

Wrong grain KPI

Revenue grouped by customer doubles after joining to a multi-address table. What is the first concern?

Why this matters

Aggregation faithfully sums its input; if join fan-out multiplied rows, KPI changes.

Provenance: extension+repo

M04

JOIN, UNION & Cardinality

M04 JOIN / UNION / Cardinality

Foundation

INNER/LEFT/RIGHT, UNION and unmatched-row behaviour.

Applied / Repo

Predict 1:1, 1:M and M:M cardinality.

Senior

Fan-out RCA, ON vs WHERE, UNION vs UNION ALL, pre/post join validation.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q027 · Ansh CP2 fixture

INNER JOIN trace

orders cust_id 101,201,501; customers id 101,201,3. INNER JOIN on cust_id=id returns how many order matches?

Why this matters

Only 101 and 201 match.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q031 · Cardinality bridge

Join multiplicity

Left row key K matches 3 right rows key K. How many output rows are produced for that left row?

Why this matters

Join emits one output row per matching pair.

Provenance: extension

SENIOR · Q036 · RCA join multiplication

DISTINCT as fan-out fix

Revenue doubles after the join. Why is `SELECT DISTINCT` not a universal fix?

Why this matters

The root cause is cardinality/business rules; DISTINCT operates on projected row equality, not relationship correctness.

Provenance: extension

M05

DML & Maintenance Safety

M05 UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / TRUNCATE / Maintenance

Foundation

UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, TRUNCATE and state changes.

Applied / Repo

Make corrections with explicit predicates and safe scope.

Senior

Retry/idempotency, partial rerun, transaction/recovery reasoning.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q041 · Ansh CP3

UPDATE scope

`UPDATE customers SET name="sam" WHERE id=101` changes?

Why this matters

WHERE scopes the UPDATE to matching rows.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q043 · Ansh CP3

Trace state update then delete

CP3 updates id101 name to sam, then deletes email aa. What is the final state for id101?

Why this matters

UPDATE changes name but email remains aa; subsequent DELETE removes that row.

Provenance: source

SENIOR · Q045 · Maintenance contract

Historical correction

Need correct one month history. What is the safest principle?

Why this matters

Controlled correction requires scope, evidence, safe rerun and validation.

Provenance: extension

M06

Numeric, Date, String & CAST

M06 Numeric / Date / String / CAST

Foundation

Arithmetic, date functions, CAST and string transformations.

Applied / Repo

Normalize types/keys/time before joins and dedup.

Senior

Timezone, money precision, key-normalization and index/casting side effects.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q047 · Ansh CP3

10% discount

unit_price 200, expression unit_price*0.90 gives?

Why this matters

200×0.90=180.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q052 · Ansh CP4/5

DATE_FORMAT

`%W %M %e %Y` represents?

Why this matters

Those specifiers format full weekday/month names, day-of-month and four-digit year.

Provenance: source

SENIOR · Q057 · Type contract

Cast and join key

Joining INT customer_id to dirty VARCHAR ids with on-the-fly CAST can create what concern?

Why this matters

Type normalization should be governed upstream; runtime casts can hide bad values and affect plans.

Provenance: extension

M07

CASE & Business Rules

M07 CASE / Business Rules

Foundation

CASE ordering, ELSE and rule classification.

Applied / Repo

Encode business rules and check overlap/defaults.

Senior

Govern rule precedence, NULL/default behaviour and change impact.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q061 · Ansh CP6

CASE first match

unit_price=80. CASE WHEN <=100 affordable WHEN <=200 normal ELSE expensive. Result?

Why this matters

CASE returns first matching branch.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q063 · Ansh CP6

Rule order

Why branch order matters when conditions overlap?

Why this matters

More specific/priority conditions must be ordered intentionally.

Provenance: source+extension

SENIOR · Q065 · Pharma match tiers

CASE as hidden model

Huge CASE with many entity-resolution priorities becomes risky because?

Why this matters

Complex rules benefit from explicit data/model governance rather than buried logic.

Provenance: extension+repo bridge

M08

Window Aggregates & Frames

M08 Window Aggregates / Frames

Foundation

Window vs aggregate, running metrics and frames.

Applied / Repo

Trace row-preserving calculations.

Senior

Frame surprises, scope filtering and window-order vs final-order reasoning.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q067 · Ansh CP6

Running sum frame

ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW means?

Why this matters

Explicit ROWS frame accumulates from partition start to current row.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q069 · Ansh CP6

Trace running sum

prices ordered 10,20,30. Running sums?

Why this matters

Cumulative sums are 10;10+20=30;10+20+30=60.

Provenance: source

SENIOR · Q072 · Window input scope optimization

Filter before window

You rank full customer history then need current top event. Can filtering history first be unsafe?

Why this matters

Window semantics depend on input set; optimization cannot alter required history.

Provenance: extension

M09

Ranking, Dedup & LAG/LEAD

M09 Ranking / PARTITION / Dedup / LAG-LEAD

Foundation

ROW_NUMBER/RANK/DENSE_RANK/PARTITION/LAG/LEAD.

Applied / Repo

Choose grain + meaningful winner ordering.

Senior

Deterministic winner, total order, previous row vs previous time period.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q075 · Ansh CP6

Ranking ties

For values 100,100,200, DENSE_RANK ranks?

Why this matters

Dense rank repeats ties without gaps.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q078 · Ansh CP6 nth value

Nth most expensive direction

For “5th most expensive distinct price”, ranking order should be?

Why this matters

Most expensive requires descending price.

Provenance: source issue+correction

SENIOR · Q083 · Determinism hardening

Same timestamp conflict

Two conflicting rows have same business key and same updated_at, no sequence/priority. Best response?

Why this matters

Data may be insufficient to infer authoritative winner.

Provenance: extension

M10

Subquery, CTE, View, Procedure & Function

M10 Subquery / CTE / View / Procedure / Function

Foundation

Stage complex SQL and reusable objects.

Applied / Repo

Break transformations into understandable steps.

Senior

CTE/view assumptions, portability and maintainability boundaries.

3 guided checkpoints

FOUNDATION · Q089 · Ansh CP6

Subquery definition

A subquery is?

Why this matters

Notes introduce subquery as query within query.

Provenance: source

APPLIED · Q090 · Ansh CP6

Above-average products

Pattern `WHERE unit_price > (SELECT AVG(unit_price)...)` does?

Why this matters

Scalar subquery supplies comparison value.

Provenance: source

SENIOR · Q095 · MySQL 8.4 derived-table optimization

CTE materialization myth

Statement “CTE is always materialized and therefore faster” is?

Why this matters

MySQL can merge or materialize CTEs/derived tables; inspect plan rather than assume.

Provenance: extension verified

Final SQL gate

After all 10 modules, complete 100-question + 24-lab assessment. The target is not the score alone; you should be able to explain why the other choices are wrong and solve incidents without hints.

After SQL/Data reasoning, continue to Senior DE Operations / Platform Lab.
